title: Chapter 96: Day and Night 7
content:
Chapter 96

He saw it with agonizing clarity now: all those self-righteous promises he’d made before pouring the wine—that he wasonly going to ask questions and nothing else—had been pure, unadulterated self-delusion.

Lan Wangji was, by nature, the most upright and rigorously disciplined man alive. If getting drunk turned him petulant, aggressive, and utterly reckless, it meant alcohol stripped him of every shred of self-control. And Wei Wuxian had known this. He’d known it, yet he’d seized the opening anyway, exploiting Lan Wangji’s compromised state to prod, stroke, and deliberately fan the flames just to see how far he could push.

No matter how pure-hearted or detached Lan Wangji was, he was still a hot-blooded young man. Goading him with that kind of shameless, heavy-handed friction was practically begging for an explosion. To make matters worse, Jiang Cheng had just dragged Lan Wangji through the mud over this very thing back at Lotus Pier; on top of that, Lan Wangji was sick with worry over his missing brother. And what had Wei Wuxian done? He’d chosentonightof all nights to lose his mind and take liberties.

Lan Wangji hadn’t uttered a single syllable after that flat "Mm," but Wei Wuxian’s head was already spinning through a thousand agonizing loops.

Across two lifetimes, shame was a concept Wei Wuxian had never quite grasped. Now, it crashed over him with devastating, suffocating force. His lips still throbbed, raw and swollen, and the sticky slick of dried mess clinging to his stomach and thighs made his skin crawl. He wanted nothing more than tobash his head against the wall and die.

The fallout had confirmed his worst, most gut-wrenching fear: Lan Wangji cared for him deeply, yes. But it wasn't the kind of care Wei Wuxian was hoping for.

Desperate to save them both from drowning in humiliation, Wei Wuxian scrambled to pull his clothes back on, dragging his robes up in frantic haste. He rubbed the side of his head, forcing his voice into its usual breezy, easygoing lilt. "Well! Look at that, you're sober. Guess that makes two of us."

Lan Wangji turned, his eyes cutting straight through him. Wei Wuxian didn't dare look close enough to parse whatever storm was brewing in those pale irises; his trembling fingers fumbled blindly with his robes. Then, breaking the silence, Lan Wangji reached out toward him, his hand moving as though to help wipe away the dried, milky mess still staining Wei Wuxian’s skin.

"No, don't!" Wei Wuxian blurted out, flinching back.

Lan Wangji’s hand froze midair before slowly retreating.

Letting out a shaky breath, Wei Wuxian mumbled, "You don't need to. I've got it. Really, don't worry about touching me."

Knowing Lan Wangji, he probably thought he’d been ungentlemanly, that he bore the responsibility of tidying up the mess he'd made. But Wei Wuxian would rather die than let him clean him up now. He grabbed a discarded inner shirt, furiously scrubbing down his skin before chucking the rag aside. "Look, Lan Zhan... we probably just had a few too many tonight. My bad, really."

Lan Wangji didn't say a word.

Shoving one foot into a boot, Wei Wuxian rambled on, digging the hole deeper. "I mean, you don't have to beat yourself up over it either. Men do this sort of thing from time to time, it's totally normal. Don't... don't take it to heart, okay?"

Lan Wangji stared at him, unblinking. "Normal?"

His voice was terrifyingly flat.

Wei Wuxian froze, his throat seizing.

Lan Wangji’s voice cut through the silence again, razor-sharp. "Don't take it to heart?"

Originally, Wei Wuxian had told himself that making Lan Wangji think he was just a crass, reckless degenerate was infinitely better than laying his true feelings bare—which would only make things so excruciatingly awkward they couldn't even look each other in the eye, let alone remain friends. But watching Lan Wangji now, raw regret washed over him for blurting out such brainless drivel.

"...I'm sorry," he whispered.

Lan Wangji shot up from the bed with jarring suddenness. Panic flared in Wei Wuxian’s chest—just as a frantic set of footsteps came pounding up the wooden stairs.

A sharp knock rattled the door, followed by the landlady’s anxious call: "Young masters! Young masters! Are you awake in there?"

Lan Wangji abruptly looked away.

Scrambling to yank his other boot on, Wei Wuxian shouted, "We're awake! I mean—no, we were asleep! Hang on, let me throw a robe on!"

Once Wei Wuxian had made himself reasonably presentable, Lan Wangji finally strode over and unlatched the door.

"What's the matter?" Wei Wuxian asked.

The landlady hovered in the corridor, offering a wincing, apologetic smile. "I am so, so sorry to bother you both this late, truly! But I didn't have a choice—the folks staying right below you complained about water leaking through their ceiling, and they're worried it's coming from your room. So I just had to come check..."

She poked her head past them, and her jaw instantly dropped. "Good heavens! What on earth happened in here?!"

Wei Wuxian rubbed his jaw, offering his most charming, sheepish grin. "Ah, my fault entirely, ma'am. I had a bit too much to drink and got rowdy. Decided I wanted a bath, got carried away, smacked the wooden tub a little too hard, and... well, it kind of splintered. Really sorry about the mess. I'll pay for the damages."

The words had barely cleared his mouth when reality caught up with him:Pay with what?He didn't have two coppers to rub together. Lan Wangji had footed the bill for literally everything since they'd left the Cloud Recesses; at the end of the day, Lan Wangji was the one who was going to take the financial hit.

"Oh, it's fine, it's fine, accidents happen..." the landlady fretted, though her expression was pure agony. She stepped inside, picking her way gingerly through the puddle. "Mercy, how did it leak this badly? There's barely a dry patch to stand on..."

She bent down to scoop up a few soaked floor cushions, only to freeze, gasping anew. "Why is there a hole in the floor?!"

It was the puncture mark Lan Wangji had driven Bichen through earlier.

Wei Wuxian ran a hand through his messy hair, laying on the apologies as thick as he could. "Ah, that was me too, my bad! I was tossing my sword around for fun and, well..."

Before he could spin the lie any further, Lan Wangji bent down, retrieved his money pouch from the floorboards, and placed a hefty silver ingot onto the dry corner of the table.

The landlady’s scowl melted instantly. Still, clutching her chest, she couldn't resist a stern scolding: "Young master, I have to say, a sword is a lethal weapon! How could you go throwing it around like a toy? Gouging the floor and the mats is one thing, but what if you'd hurt someone?"

Wei Wuxian nodded like a chastised schoolboy. "Yes, yes, of course. You're completely right."

Pocketing the silver, the landlady sighed. "Well, what's done is done. It's late, so you two go get some rest. I'll move you to another room for tonight and have this patched up first thing in the morning."

"Sounds great, thank you so much for the trouble..." Wei Wuxian began, then caught himself. "Wait! Actually... could we get two rooms, please?"

The landlady blinked, confused. "Two? Weren't you sharing?"

Wei Wuxian didn't dare look Lan Wangji in the eye. He kept his head down, mumbling, "...I get reckless when I drink. You saw it yourself—smashing tubs, throwing blades around. Don't want to risk hurting anyone."

"Ah," she nodded sagely. "Fair point!"

True to her word, she quickly arranged a pair of adjoining rooms. Once they were settled, she gathered her skirts and hurried back downstairs.

Wei Wuxian murmured his thanks, pushing open the door to his new quarters. He paused, looking back over his shoulder.

Lan Wangji remained standing in the dimly lit hallway. Bichen was clasped in one hand, while the fingers of his other gently smoothed down the tails of his forehead ribbon, his head bowed in deep, unreadable silence. Wei Wuxian had meant to duck inside and hide, but the sight rooted his boots to the floorboards.

Weighing every syllable with agonizing care, he offered a quiet, tentative apology. "Lan Zhan... about tonight. I'm sorry."

After a long stretch of silence, Lan Wangji spoke, his voice barely above a whisper. "You never need to say those words to me."

He adjusted his forehead ribbon until it sat immaculate, straight, and centered. In an instant, the peerless, inviolable Hanguang-jun was back.

He gave a slight, formal nod. "Rest well. We will discuss the Guanyin Temple and Lanling tomorrow."

Hearing those final words, the suffocating weight in Wei Wuxian’s chest eased just a fraction. At the very least, there was still a tomorrow to discuss together.

Forcing a small smile, he nodded. "Yeah. You too. Get some sleep, and we'll figure it out tomorrow."
